info.title: Affinidi DID Hosting — edge HTTP surface
info.description: HTTP surface of the did-hosting-server edge node: public, unauthenticated DID resolution, a liveness probe, and the HTTPS binding of the Trust Task listener. The edge is written to only by its control plane's signed Trust Tasks, which arrive over TSP, DIDComm or this binding alike.

get.description:
The FAQ gives a name with an empty local part to the verifiable trust
community that owns the domain, and in this service the domain's own
identity is its root DID. So this resolves through exactly the same index
as every other name: nothing special-cases the root slot here, because
`validate_agent_name_binding` has already made `.well-known` the only
mnemonic the empty name can be bound to.

Needs a separate handler only because a path parameter cannot capture an
empty segment — `/@` never matches `/@{name}`.

302.description: Redirect; `Location` is the domain's root DID (the community name)

404.description: No community name bound, or `features.agent_names` is off

429.description: This address's resolution rate exceeds `[server.resolve_rate_limit]`; see `Retry-After`

get.description:
The optional `context` tail (`/@alice/h2hsummit`) is accepted and ignored
for the redirect target — it is the FAQ's context-path affordance, carried
through for the caller's benefit, not part of the name's identity.

get.summary:
Unauthenticated liveness probe; degraded while the service's own DID is
not being served.

200.description: Service is up and its own DID (if configured) resolves locally; returns status + version

503.description: Service is up but its own DID isn't being served locally, or it has not reconciled with its control plane within the staleness bound

post.summary:
Hand the posted document to the edge's one inbound dispatch and answer with
its signed reply.
post.description:
A document that fails `verify_control_plane` gets no answer, signed or
unsigned: a signed refusal would settle a directive the control plane never
sent, and an error document is an answer too. It is refused with a bare
`403` and an empty body, as is a document that takes no reply. One that
could not be checked just now (its signer's DID could not be resolved, the
replay cache is full) is answered `503` with `Retry-After` and an empty
body, so the sender keeps it and sends it again.

400.description: The body is not a Trust Task document

403.description: The document was not accepted, or takes no reply; empty body

408.description: The body did not arrive in time

413.description: The body is larger than the listener accepts

429.description: This address's request rate exceeds the limit

503.description: The document could not be checked just now; send it again after `Retry-After`. Empty body
